apk_audit_v01_duplicate_content_encoding.why_it_matters: The standards finding changes the repair's justification, not just its wording. RFC 9110 s8.4 defines Content-Encoding as a list (#content-coding), so repeated Content-Encoding is legal HTTP/1.1 input: refusing it is a deliberate strictness, and RLLM already chooses that strictness on the final head at three surfaces and in the frame session. So the fix is consistency with an existing product policy, not the invention of a new rule, and it must not silently widen into rejecting a legal single-field coding list. The live risk the card names is parser disagreement plus a silent decode change if a coding is ever applied from an interim or redirect head, where today no coding is applied and no guard exists.

mark_anchor_dir_fsync_open: OPEN P2 found by the mark1 seat and confirmed by me: rewrite_mark syncs the temp FILE (sync_all) but never syncs the parent DIRECTORY after rename. Appending to an existing file needs no dir sync; a rename changes the directory, so after power loss the rename can be lost while the companion append survives, leaving the anchor one append stale (or absent). Consequence is a weaker witness, never a false pass, because append_linked validates the recorded chain (:1586 recorded_successor_revisions, :1592 successor_chain_break) before append_mark (:1598). measured_state.turn_lifetime_adjudication: MM4's item (1) taken by the coordinator with instruments after that seat wedged at launch. Four questions, all answered from source with the pinned tree, each now a named check in verification/turn_background.rs (the .py leg was deleted by a9e8f11; citation corrected 2026-11-14). (A) OUTLIVING: the promotion and the wake lock cannot outlive the turn by two independent bounds - TurnService.finish() is reached on every turn-ending path (Activity.java:265 model result/failure clears turnActive then finishes; :757 stopped; :769 publishReply; :1208 onDestroy) and independently wake.acquire(lease) carries its own timeout while the ticker's 'if(elapsed>=lease){stopSelf();return;}' drives onDestroy, which clears active, removeCallbacksAndMessages, stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE) and release(). Every onStartCommand path returns START_NOT_STICKY, so a killed service is not resurrected without a fresh begin(). (B) STRANDING: cannot happen either, because the lease and the socket deadline are the same window - turnLease (Activity.java:730) = max(30000,min(600000,optLong("timeout_ms",120000))) and the transport deadline for the same effect (:611) = started+max(5000,min(600000,optLong("timeout_ms",120000))); one default (120000), one cap (600000). Pinned by the check 'the promotion window and the request transport window share one default and one cap so the wake lock can neither outlive nor strand the turn'. (C) WHAT SETS THE WINDOW: measured, not assumed - grep of core/ finds exactly one emitter of timeout_ms, core/services.rs:182 (the service/job dispatch; its purpose is a service_request:<ts> ticket), and the model effect (core/application.rs:909, and the hosted-search continuation at :785) carries NO timeout key, so turnLease always resolves to the 120000 default and its 30s-600s clamp never moves. This corrects this ledger's and AUDIT.md's earlier wording that the lease is 'taken from the turn's own request timeout'. Consequence the owner should see: in the shipped Android surface a model request cannot run longer than 120s end-to-end (the same default bounds socket connect, soTimeout and the wake lock), so a provider slower than that is cut off before the lease is the limit. (D) SHARED PROMOTION: yes by design - TurnService.begin reuses the live instance ('if(service!=null&&service.active){service.extend(ticket,started,lease,label);return;}') and onStartCommand re-enters extend() when already active, so a chained model effect (harness retry, hosted-search continuation) rewrites ticket/label/started/lease and re-acquires the lock on the SAME promotion instead of stacking a second one; turnActive is a single volatile boolean, so the Activity never runs two model turns concurrently. (E) REPLY LOSS: the reply is committed to encrypted history before any notification leg, so no conversation data is lost between settle and delivery; what can be lost is the announcement - publishPendingReply is gated by TurnService.notificationsAllowed, so on API 33+ with POST_NOTIFICATIONS denied a backgrounded user gets no signal even though the reply landed (drains: the permission-result callback code==56 and openRequestedConversation on resume). Left as a DEVICE-ACCEPTANCE caveat, not closed here. Not measured: the narrow main-thread race where a begin() lands after the ticker's stopSelf() but before onDestroy (current!=null && active still true -> extend() on a stopping service, so the new turn would run unpromoted); it needs a device or a harness that can order those callbacks, and no source-level instrument can settle it.

snapshot_identity_native_tls_lane_2026_1.repair_rfc5746: Two halves, both measured. (1) Indication: RFC 5746 section 3.3 lets a client signal secure renegotiation with the TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV value 0x00ff *inside its cipher-suite list* instead of the renegotiation_info (0xff01) extension; OpenSSL 3.0 sends only the SCSV. The lane parsed the extension and never looked at the suite list, so it treated every OpenSSL client as renegotiation-unsafe. Added `pub const SCSV_SECURE_RENEGOTIATION: u16 = 0x00ff` (verification/snapshot_identity.rs:1180) and `let mut renegotiation_info = cipher_suites.contains(&SCSV_SECURE_RENEGOTIATION);` in ClientHello::parse (:1250). (2) Echo: a new `server_hello_body` emits the renegotiation_info extension with extension_data of exactly one 0x00 byte (section 3.4: an empty renegotiated_connection), plus EMS zero-length and ec_point_formats [1,0]. A half-fix that emitted zero-length extension_data was measured red with `tls_parse_stoc_renegotiate:renegotiation encoding err` before the 0x00 byte was restored. Final: all three arms rc=0, full record sequence ClientHello -> ServerHello -> Certificate -> ServerKeyExchange -> ServerHelloDone -> ClientKeyExchange -> CCS, and `CMP-events: identical` against the python fixture's captured request under the same OpenSSL client.

Python legs quote their report path; a twin derives its filename from verification/twin/mod.rs::group_report_file(group), so the name appears nowhere in its source and the row printed `services PASS (exit 0, 0s, unparsed checks)`. The fix passes the harness's own group_report_file(name) into file_measure as a canonical report name, and clears that report before the group runs so its presence afterwards is the proof of execution. The sweep path (sweep_one) already derived the report path itself and is untouched. Counted gained #[derive(Debug)]. B01's shape: the comment-aware scanner stopped at the FIRST occurrence of the block-comment terminator, so a token inside the outer of two nested Rust block comments could still decide (a) a native dispatch via native_accepts_flag and (b) a native required-input read. Its BASE line pins are find_outside block arm :86 (chars[at+2..].windows(2).position(|pair| pair == ['*','/'])), find_outside_comments block arm :135 (same scan), find_outside_comments :120, contains_outside_comments :183, and the decision sites :653 with reads :657-:659 and :486

the compiler fact that grounds it: rustc 1.95.0 compiles a statement placed inside a nested block comment (exit 0, 0 B stderr) while the same statement as code errors E0308 — so a non-nesting scanner diverges from the language on a construct that is legal source

a_parent_audits_blocking_finding_is_a_pi.conclusion: A parent audit's blocking finding is most useful to the child re-audit as a pinning inventory: the arms it lists define the completeness sweep (a single surviving first-terminator-wins arm in the delivered bytes is BLOCKING), and the decision sites it lists define where a probe must assert. That is why the re-audit brief restates the pins and requires the seat to hunt surviving arms rather than re-read the parent's prose, and why the probe legs require positive controls (a token in a real string literal must still be accepted) so a scanner that simply stops matching cannot pass green.

the_porcelain_line_count_is_not_a_dirty_.conclusion: Two consequences, both load-bearing for lane arithmetic. (1) A room built with git ls-files -z | tar copies INDEX paths with WORKING-TREE bytes, so it carries the 18 modified product files as live bytes and carries NONE of the 11 untracked entries — a room has no .qwen/fleet, no bloat, no APK, and none of the resource-owner residue dirs. unit_runner_has_no_process_group_primiti.why_it_matters: A claim about what a SIGKILL leaves behind is only true of the runner that actually terminates the leg in question. Any future wording about a scratch-tree ceiling must name which runner, and any janitor/reclaim design must know that a unit-test child is killed directly, so its whole process survives the kill only as the units binary itself.
